Dynamic live-region height shipped as src/viewport.rs (policy + mechanics), wired into the frame loop in src/main.rs; the compile-time VIEWPORT_H is gone.

POLICY. desired_height(mode, term_rows, preview_rows, tool_rows) = chrome (status 1 + input 3) + the live text rows that actually want the screen, floored at chrome+1 (a frame that cannot show its input box is broken) and capped by MAX_LIVE_ROWS (40) plus a KEEP_SCROLLBACK_ROWS (3) margin so the live region reads as a pane inside a transcript instead of eating the window. Beads and Pi are prose and grow. Bash keeps a deliberately small fixed region - one live preview row - and it is documented in the module docs as the ticket requires: complete lines of shell output go straight to the scrollback as the transcript's own lines (ADR-0001 rule 1), so only the partial line the shell has not finished is live; a program that paints a screen takes the whole terminal via the `screen` passthrough (ADR-0001 Q2) and nothing of ours is drawn.

MECHANICS. ratatui 0.30 gives no setter for the viewport (Viewport::Inline(h) is read from a private field), so a new height means a new Terminal over a backend still looking at the same stdout. LiveView::fit parks the cursor on the live region's own top row, erases everything below it, and rebuilds. Growing scrolls by exactly the shortfall and lands the new viewport under the last line already written; shrinking cannot scroll at all, so flushed lines keep the rows they had. The erase is not tidiness: a fresh Terminal diffs against a blank back buffer, so a cell blank in the new frame but not on screen is last frame's text welded there for the session. Rows above the live region's top are never touched - asserted cell by cell against TestBackend.

FOUND WHILE MEASURING (kept, because it was on the acceptance path). Every cursor query an inline rebuild needs (ESC[6n) races the async key stream for the same stdin: if the stream is alive it eats the answer and the query waits out crossterm's 2s timeout. The frame loop therefore (1) stops the key stream across fit / resize_window, gated by needs_fit so a frame that changes nothing does not pay for a restart, (2) polls the real window size with an ioctl each frame - a SIGWINCH that lands while the stream is stopped is never delivered at all, and ratatui's own autoresize would otherwise resize mid-draw, i.e. query with the stream running - and (3) treats neither a failed shape change nor a failed frame as fatal: fit keeps the old height (needs_fit stays true, next frame retries from the same parked cursor) and a draw that failed did so in autoresize before swapping buffers, so there is nothing inconsistent to recover from.

Scrollback store landed. The transcript is no longer printed anywhere: it is held
per view in `src/state/scrollback.rs` and drawn as a window onto that store.

WHAT IS BUILT
- `Scrollback { rows, width, offset, pinned, pending, dropped, max_rows }`.
  `offset` is rows hanging between the bottom of the view and the tail; `pinned`
  is `offset == 0`, cached and written only by `set_offset` so the two cannot
  disagree; `pending` is the count of rows that arrived while unpinned and is the
  only data source behind the "N new" affordance; `max_rows` defaults to 4096 and
  `dropped` makes the trim a counted thing for looprs-pdl.7 to read. No absolute
  scroll position anywhere: every question the frame asks is relative to the tail.
- ADR-0004 R14's provenance per row: `DisplayRow { entry, logical, start, end:
  RowEnd, line, cells: CellMap }`. `entry` is re-based by `entries_evicted` so a
  byte trim cannot leave a row addressing a stranger (tested: `eviction_leaves_no
  _row_the_transcript_cannot_re_render`); `end` is the hard-vs-soft flag that
  `paste_text` turns into the copy join (soft inserts nothing, hard inserts exactly
  one \n) so a copied paragraph does not read as if it were typed with a stuck
  Enter; `cells` is a map of `CellSpan { cell, cells, start, end }` in *cluster*
  units, which is what looprs-pdl.9 needs to snap a cell range without emitting
  half a CJK glyph or half a ZWJ family (tested across CJK, combining marks and a
  ZWJ family).
- Styles are kept on the row and never copied — looprs-pdl.5's "decode SGR"
  decision honoured rather than half-implemented. `styles_render_and_are_never_co
  pied` is that rule as a test: the row that paints yellow lands in `paste_text`
  as plain text.
- Scroll semantics in the store, not spread across callers: `pinned_is_the_defaul
  t_and_new_output_follows`, `scrolling_up_one_row_unpins`,
  `unpinned_holds_its_content_and_counts_what_arrived`,
  `reaching_the_very_bottom_re_pins_and_clears_the_count`,
  `cannot_scroll_past_the_top_of_the_content`.
- Re-wrap anchored on content: `rewrap` records the resting row as
  `ContentAnchor { entry, logical, byte }` before the re-render and finds it
  after (`rewrap_anchors_on_content_not_on_row_index`). When the anchor's entry is
  gone the store holds rather than inventing a position
  (`rewrap_with_lost_content_holds_rather_than_inventing_a_position`).

WHAT CHANGED AROUND IT
- `md::wrap` returns `Wrapped { line, soft }` so the wrap verdict travels with
  the row instead of being re-inferred from the last element by every caller;
  `render_markdown_tracked` alongside the old entry point.
- `SessionView::display: Vec<Line>` is `scrollback: Scrollback`. `flush(width)`
  drains at the width the frame will draw at and, if the width moved, re-wraps the
  whole store first — and does not then push the freshly drained rows a second
  time, because the re-wrap already made them (this was the one real bug found on
  the way: the first flush after a width change returned empty).
- `App::transcript_window(visible)` answers with the slice the offset says;
  `TranscriptBand` takes `&[DisplayRow]` and draws that and nothing else, so the
  band no longer keeps a second, shallower copy of the transcript.
- The live tail shows only while the view follows the tail. Scrolled up, the band
  belongs to the history; a live line under the rows the user stopped on would
  redraw the thing they are reading on every delta.
- The "N new" affordance (`NewRowsPill`) is an **overlay** on the band's bottom
  row — the row the tail would be on — not a row of its own, for exactly the
  reason ADR-0004 R21 gives for the copy toast: an affordance that reserves a row
  reshapes the text below it on every arrival.
- `App::height` is tracked (from the startup size and every Resize event) so a
  "page" is the band `viewport::frame_areas` actually lays out rather than a
  second arithmetic that can drift. PageUp/PageDown/Home/End are wired to
  `Scrollback`; claimed because `InputState::handle_key` ignores all four, so
  taking them moves no keystroke off the box (asserted). The chord table,
  including what Home/End mean once there is a Ctrl-C nobody has stolen, stays
  looprs-pdl.13's.

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE, as the ticket required
The Flusher's markdown/fence/raw-line logic: untouched, same rendering rules, in
the same file, returning `Vec<Wrapped>`/`RenderedRow` instead of plain `Line`s.
The live-preview/flush split is intact — `App::flush_active` still happens inside
the branch that draws, with the width that frame will draw at, before the preview
is taken. The entry model is untouched.

Drag selection model + wiring landed. src/state/selection.rs: CharRef/CharRange address the selection by (entry, logical line, byte) so it is a fact about content, not about cells; press/drag/release with the click-clears rule; the range normalises direction; endpoints snap to whole clusters through the store's CellMap (never half a CJK glyph or ZWJ family); soft folds and hard newlines follow the store's own join rule via paste_slices (ADR-0004 R14/R15); auto-scroll 1 row / 100ms at the band edges; entries_evicted mirrors the store's renumbering and clears when the trim ate the anchor. Wired: view() publishes a BandSnapshot of the frame it drew (components::text_stream::band_layout is now the band's single layout opinion, shared by the draw, the snapshot and the tests) so the pointer maps to the pixels rather than to a second guess; App::on_mouse drives press/drag/release, scrolls before re-reading the pointer, and re-publishes the snapshot after an auto-scroll so the selection keeps growing past the edge; the first Esc unselects and emits no Cancel, the next is the normal cancel; Tab and a full-screen child take it out of play; the eviction seam (SessionView::take_trims -> App::sync_selection_to_trims, called from flush_active and after update_inner) keeps the addresses honest when the buffer cap bites. Highlight is a Modifier::REVERSED toggle over the band, drawn under the chrome, that re-derives from the character range every frame and reflows nothing (frame-level test: chrome rows byte-identical, whole frame text unchanged). Mouse scroll landed: the trio is on by default through the ledger, the wheel drives the store, and the burst is rate-limited.

ACCEPTANCE, CRITERION BY CRITERION
1. 1000+1002+1006 enabled/disabled as ONE unit via the mode ledger. Mode::DEFAULT (src/teardown.rs) now carries all three, so they go on through exit.enable at startup and come back off under the same restore that hands back the screen -- exactly once each, on every path including the panic one (measured: one `h` and one `l` per mode in the capture, spike group 1). The unit rule is enforced both ways: LOOPRS_MODES=-mouse drops all three together, and a partial removal (-mouse_sgr) is refused by resolve_group, because 1002 without 1006 is coordinates that wrap past column 223. Nothing else in DEFAULT can be declined (-raw/-alt_screen error: the app has no shape without them).
2. Wheel and trackpad scroll the transcript by a DOCUMENTED row delta citing the measured burst shape. WHEEL_ROWS_PER_STEP = 3 whole rows, WHEEL_STEP_INTERVAL = 60 ms = 50 rows/s, both in src/state/wheel.rs with the measurements next to them: pdl.2 #4a (128 reports in one write, 0.301 ms, ~4.3e5 ev/s -- the wire is never the limit), pdl.2 #4b quoted as still NOT MEASURED (no finger on this path), and the cadence this ticket did measure through the running app (spikes/mouse_scroll_e2e.py / spikes/results/mouse-scroll-e2e.log): one notch = 3 rows and 3 back; a timed burst of 40 reports over 299 ms = 15 rows at 50.2 rows/s against the ceiling, bound recomputed from the duration measured. The rate is the design, not a multiplier: the burst's report count carries no intent, its duration does -- which is why a notch is never rounded to one row and a flick never reads forty. A real finger can still retune without a code change: the cadence logs reports/duration/rows per gesture (`grep 'wheel gesture closed' looprs.log`).
3. Events over the input/status bands do not scroll. BandSnapshot::contains_row is the frame's own answer about where the band is, so the box, the status row and the card band own the cursor over them (unit: a_wheel_over_the_input_box_or_the_status_row_does_not_scroll_the_transcript, the_live_card_band_is_not_transcript_and_does_not_scroll; pty: group 5 -- no row of the band moves).
4. No scroll-state change while a child holds the screen. App::on_wheel returns before touching anything when passthrough() is set -- the same rule the drag has -- so neither the offset nor the pin moves and no frame is asked for (no_wheel_state_changes_while_a_child_holds_the_screen). Capture does not fight the child's: the re-assert the App writes on the way back is the ledger's own held set, which now includes all three mouse modes, so after a mouse-tracking vim (pdl.2 #7 kills our modes on exit) the wheel comes back on its own.
5. No idle frame cost when the mouse is still. The frame is marked dirty only when the store actually moved: a wheel at either end and every throttled report inside a burst cost a comparison and nothing else, and with no movement there is no draw (unit: a_wheel_at_the_end_of_the_transcript_costs_no_frame, the throttled half of a_trackpad_burst_at_the_app_door_is_throttled_not_queued; pty: group 6 -- 0 bytes over 2s with the mouse still, 467 bytes for one notch, 0 again after the gesture drained). No new timers: the reports arrive on the existing EventStream as Msg::Term(Event::Mouse(_)).

The ticket was right about the symptom and the DESIGN's first hypothesis was the correct one: Event::Resize never arrives under the pty harness -- SIGWINCH is delivered to the foreground process group of the terminal's SESSION, and a Popen(stdin=slave) spike never makes the pty the child's controlling terminal. Guards: one unreadable size retires the poll for the run (crossterm falls back to spawning tput), 0x0 is never adopted. WHERE. Two halves, because two things had to be true and only one of them is rendering. THE RULES, AS BUILT. One shared header row (viewport::KANBAN_HEADER_ROWS), so a column gets height - header - footer rows and not less. The header count is read off the snapshot, so it is the true total and cannot drift with what the frame had room for; where a column is too narrow for the count whole, no count is drawn rather than a truncated one. The +N more marker is one of the rows, not an extra one: rows=4 with ten beads draws 3 beads and "+7 more", and shown + N closes on the total — tested at 1, 2, 3 and 5 body rows, each with totals at the boundary, one over, three over and ten over, with the expectation computed independently of the widget. The marker is laid out before the title is truncated and the id before the title: at one column wide the marker is the thing that survives, alone. An empty column draws a dim em dash — but only when a read answered; after an error the column is not drawn, because the alternative asserts the state of a board that failed to read. Never-loaded paints header-with-em-dashes plus "reading the board…"; a failed read keeps its last good rows, dims them, and says its own words with the age of the read they came from ("bd failed (exit 3): repository lock held by pid 4211 · stale 1m13s"). The footer gives up its sentence before it gives up its freshness tails.

PURITY. The component is a pure function of snapshot + area: no clock, no env, no bd call, no channel. The age arrives on the snapshot from whoever holds the clock. Failure keeps the last good rows plus the error variant, the age of the last good read keeps counting while failing, and a later success clears it; never_loaded / empty / broken are three distinct answers. Drop aborts the task and bd::run's kill_on_drop(true) reaps any mid-flight child; the board is dropped before the shutdown drain because it is the one thing still able to start a process on the way out. 17 tests, all against the injected fake bd (start/stop markers give bd_max_con()==1 with a 350ms fake on a 100ms interval), so no real board or network is reachable. Cadence is measured between the producer's fetched_at stamps, not arrival times — see memory looprs-timing-tests. The band itself is not wired; that is looprs-5o4.5.
